- Changing documented timeout exit-code behavior

## Specs

- specs/coding-testing-standards.html §5-7, §9

title: Bound --items-cmd stdout capture and fail cleanly on oversized batches
description:

## Steps to Reproduce
- Run the baseline with `--items-cmd` producing a very large stdout batch.
- Observe that AFK captures the entire batch before parsing.
- There is no guardrail that fails cleanly before memory use grows without bound.

## Scope
- Size-bounded `--items-cmd` stdout capture with a fixed internal limit
- Clear stderr failure reporting when the limit is exceeded
- Regression coverage for discard/failure behavior

## Out of scope
- Adding a new user-facing CLI flag for the limit
- Broad streaming-parser redesign
- Parse-path performance tuning unrelated to the safety limit

## Specs
- specs/prd-afk.html §5-6, §10-11
- specs/architecture.html §8-10, §12-13
- specs/coding-testing-standards.html §5-7, §9

## Wires up
- Dynamic item-source capture before item parsing

## Acceptance Criteria
- Oversized `--items-cmd` output no longer grows memory without bound before AFK reacts
- When the fixed internal limit is exceeded, AFK exits `1`, emits a clear stderr diagnostic, and does not parse the partial batch as items
- Existing non-zero/timeout discard behavior remains intact, and no new CLI flag is introduced
